conflicts.description: The same broad person/performer concept is named name in IMDb and actor in Sakila, with different identifier and name-column conventions.
conflicts.resolution: A unified person resource was created. Source identifiers feed person_id, while IMDb display_name remains distinct from Sakila's atomic first_name and last_name because they are not semantically interchangeable.

conflicts.description: Audiovisual works are called titles in IMDb and films in Sakila; title columns also use primarytitle versus title.
conflicts.resolution: The entities were unified as work, and equivalent display-title values were named primary_title.

conflicts.description: IMDb calls work classifications genres while Sakila calls them categories.
conflicts.resolution: Both are represented by neutral classification and work_classification resources.

conflicts.description: Equivalent duration attributes use different names.
conflicts.resolution: They were unified as runtime_seconds.

conflicts.description: IMDb alphanumeric identifiers are incorrectly declared as number in several source resources despite descriptions specifying strings.
conflicts.resolution: All alphanumeric IMDb identifiers are represented as string.

conflicts.description: IMDb primarytitle is declared integer although its description defines textual content.
conflicts.resolution: primary_title is typed string.

conflicts.description: Calendar years are represented as strings in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Valid years are typed integer, with source null sentinels treated as missing values.

conflicts.description: Durations and monetary amounts are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Durations are numeric integer seconds and monetary values are number, without inventing an unavailable currency.

conflicts.description: Boolean status flags are encoded as strings.
conflicts.resolution: The target uses boolean is_active fields.

conflicts.description: Source fields described as date-and-time values are typed date.
conflicts.resolution: The target uses datetime for event timestamps.

conflicts.description: Foreign-key columns use integer while their referenced source primary keys are declared string.
conflicts.resolution: Target foreign and primary key types are consistently string.

conflicts.description: Runtime is stored in minutes rather than the target's standard physical unit.
conflicts.resolution: Runtime is standardized to SI seconds.

conflicts.description: Rental duration is expressed in days.
conflicts.resolution: Rental duration is standardized to SI seconds.

conflicts.description: IMDb average user rating is a numeric preference score, while Sakila rating is a categorical audience content classification.
conflicts.resolution: The semantically distinct values remain separate as average_user_rating and content_rating.

conflicts.description: IMDb alias language is a free code or label, whereas Sakila uses a keyed language entity for a film's language.
conflicts.resolution: Alias language remains language_code on work_alias; Sakila film language relationships use language_id and are not conflated.

conflicts.description: IMDb supplies a credited display name, while Sakila separates legal-style given and family names.
conflicts.resolution: display_name, first_name, and last_name remain distinct to avoid asserting equivalence between different name semantics.

conflicts.description: IMDb startyear can mean series start year, while Sakila release_year is a film release year.
conflicts.resolution: The unified attribute is explicitly named release_start_year to preserve the shared inception-year meaning without implying every work is a film.

conflicts.description: Multiple source columns contain arrays or multi-value content inside scalar strings.
conflicts.resolution: Values were atomized into person_profession, person_known_work, work_classification, work_alias_type, work_alias_attribute, work_credit, and work_special_feature rows.

conflicts.description: Credits are decomposed differently: IMDb has principal-credit rows plus director/writer arrays, while Sakila has a film-actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: All are normalized into work_credit with foreign keys to work and person and optional role-specific attributes.

conflicts.description: Sakila duplicates title and description in a separate full-text support table.
conflicts.resolution: Semantically identical film_text attributes are merged into work rather than preserving a duplicate entity.

conflicts.description: A point geometry is carried as one non-generic composite string.
conflicts.resolution: It is split into atomic numeric latitude and longitude fields compatible with generic Frictionless types.

conflicts.description: Episode hierarchy is stored as a relationship table separate from title basics.
conflicts.resolution: A normalized episode subtype/relationship resource references work twice, once for the episode and once for its parent.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds up to three genres in each title row, while Sakila models a many-to-many film-category relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Both are represented as the N:M work_classification bridge.

conflicts.description: IMDb embeds a one-to-many list of known works in each person row.
conflicts.resolution: The list is represented as person_known_work, allowing multiple works per person and multiple people per work.

conflicts.description: Contributor relationships vary between arrays, ordered principal rows, and an explicit many-to-many actor bridge.
conflicts.resolution: A row-per-person-per-credit representation is used in work_credit; repeated characters can produce separate atomic credit rows.

conflicts.description: Each alias can have multiple types and multiple descriptive attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Separate one-to-many child resources preserve each atomic type and attribute.

conflicts.description: Ratings are conceptually optional one-to-one data for a work but are stored in a separate resource without an explicit primary key.
conflicts.resolution: work_rating uses work_id as its primary key and foreign key, enforcing at most one aggregate rating row per work.

conflicts.description: Unified people have incompatible source key domains: IMDb natural-style alphanumeric identifiers and Sakila surrogate actor identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Both source primary keys map to string person_id, with source-system identity retained during integration to prevent collisions.

conflicts.description: Unified works use different source identifiers and key styles.
conflicts.resolution: Both primary keys map to string work_id, with source-system identity retained during integration.

conflicts.description: title_akas has no declared primary key although ordering is documented as unique within a title.
conflicts.resolution: work_alias uses the composite key work_id plus alias_order.

conflicts.description: title_episode has no declared primary key even though each episode work has one parent-series relationship.
conflicts.resolution: episode_work_id is the primary key and also a foreign key to work.

conflicts.description: title_ratings lacks a declared primary key despite containing one aggregate row per title.
conflicts.resolution: work_id is used as the work_rating primary key.

conflicts.description: payment has no declared primary key although payment_id is described as its unique surrogate identifier.
conflicts.resolution: payment_id is promoted to the required target primary key.

conflicts.description: Sakila bridge tables declare foreign keys but no primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized bridges use relationship-based keys where the relationship is unique; work_credit instead uses a synthetic credit_id because richer IMDb credits can repeat a work-person pair.

conflicts.description: Store and staff form a cyclic foreign-key dependency.
conflicts.resolution: Both relationships are retained because they represent different semantics: a store's manager and a staff member's home store.
